title: Just how much have energy costs raised core inflation?

segments: AI stock downturn and bubble debate
Nvidia export controls and government policy
Energy prices spilling into core inflation
Holiday retail shopping and consumer spending
SpaceX debt offering backed by AI chips
summary.headline: Nvidia drops 13.8% in broad tech rout; energy costs add up to 0.6 percentage points to core PCE inflation
summary.tldr: Major stock indices dropped sharply as high-flying artificial intelligence shares pulled back, with Nvidia falling 13.8% and the Nasdaq sinking 5.3%. Meanwhile, research from the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas indicates that elevated fuel and energy costs are spilling into core PCE inflation, contributing between 0.2 and 0.6 percentage points. In food markets, global salmon producers are hitting biological capacity limits, signaling an end to cheap farmed salmon.

key_points.point: Higher diesel and fuel costs spill over into non-energy goods and services, adding an estimated 0.2 to 0.6 percentage points to core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation.
key_points.why_it_matters: Central banks monitor core inflation to determine interest rate policy, so persistent energy price pass-throughs can prolong high interest rates.

key_points.point: Stock markets suffered severe losses, with the Nasdaq dropping 5.3%, the S&P 500 down 3.7%, Nvidia falling 13.8%, and AMD dropping 13.25%.
key_points.why_it_matters: Rapidly expanding AI infrastructure spending faces scrutiny when corporate revenues do not keep pace with massive capital investments.

key_points.point: US retail sales rose nearly 7% year-over-year in October as retailers launched early Black Friday promotions to spur demand.
key_points.why_it_matters: Retailers are attempting to capture market share early because inflation-conscious shoppers are becoming more selective with discretionary purchases.

key_points.point: Global salmon production is hitting ecological and regulatory limits in key regions like Norway and Chile, with quarterly production down about 3%.
key_points.why_it_matters: When physical supply constraints prevent market expansion, previously affordable consumer goods transform into higher-priced luxury items.

summary.lesson: When fuel and freight costs increase, transportation and manufacturing companies pass those expenses down the supply chain, causing core inflation to rise even after excluding direct consumer energy purchases.
opinions_and_predictions: Sudeep Reddy (MS Now) thinks the downturn in tech shares is an overdue market reckoning caused by unsustainable overbuilding in AI infrastructure.
Catherine Rampell (The Bulwark) expects recurring cycles of inflation and deflation in AI asset prices due to uncertainty over long-term profitability.
Olu Sonola (Fitch Ratings) expects business pricing power to persist until consumer demand weakens significantly.

glossary.definition: An inflation index tracking consumer prices for goods and services while excluding volatile food and energy prices.
glossary.example: Core PCE was listed at 3.1% last month before accounting for energy price spillover.

glossary.definition: Government regulations restricting the sale of specified advanced technologies or products to foreign nations.
glossary.example: The US Commerce Department enforces export controls on advanced AI microchips shipped abroad.

glossary.definition: A statutory ceiling established by Congress limiting the total money the federal government can borrow.
glossary.example: The US debt limit requires legislative action to avoid a potential government default.
